raw_comment:
We notice that American adults, to different degrees depending on the activity, spent an increasing amount of time at home over the past two decades. Religious and spiritual activities increased the most in terms of time spent at home. The activities that are most likely to bring people out of their homes are work and exercise., and leisure time was the activity most likely to draw people home.
    
    We wonder what this graph looks like with different demographics and in other countries. We also wonder if this increasing time spent at home was due to COVID. We are also curious about why people practiced religion increasingly at home in recent decades. 
    
    This relates to us because we’re in the age range of those surveyed, and we can see our choices and those of our parents reflected somewhat in this graph. 
    
    Catchy Titles:
    
    There’s No Place Like Home: Americans are Spending More Time at Home
    Living the 21st Century from the Comfort of Home
    America, Home of the Couch Potato
    Pray from your Couth: Americans time at Home Surges

raw_comment:
Thanks to all the students who responded, especially to other students.   Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  "Home Is the New Hub: How Our Time Is Shifting" by Ricardo of Perth Amboy High School in N.J., “The Shift to Homebodies: How Americans Have Spent Their Time Over the Years” by Lillie of Barnstable High School in Mass., “The Shift from Going Out to Staying In” by Elizabeth of Gull Lake High School in Richland, Mich., “Happy Home: Home Activities of Americans Have Increased from 2003 to 2022” by Kristina of Pewaukee, Wis. and two headlines from Academy of Saint Elizabeth in Convent Station, N.J.:  "Spending Time at Home: The Aftermath of Quarantine?" by Avery and “Modern American Homes: A School, Office, and Church In One!” by Jackie.
    
    Please return on Friday when we will reveal the free link to the article, a summary of the article, additional questions, shout outs for some of the best headlines for the graph and Stat Nuggets -- definitions of words that relate to the graph and where you can find them in the graph.
    
    The next graph will be released by Friday, January 17.  The topic will be an idea of how to make the world’s children smarter.
     
    Signing off – Sharon Hessney from Boston who definitely spends more time at home now than before the pandemic and Ben Kirk of Ithaca, N.Y.

raw_comment:
One thing that stood out to me is how much participation in religion and spirituality at home has grown since 2003, jumping from about 25% to around 60% in 2022. This is the largest increase in any activity on the graph. I also noticed that all of the activities listed have seen growth over time. Leisure not on a computer has the highest percentage overall, reaching about 85% in 2022. That surprised me, especially considering how much technology, like computers and other devices, dominates our lives now. With COVID-19, people across the U.S. and the world spent more time at home, adjusting to a new way of life, which might explain why all these activities saw a rise in at-home participation.
    It makes me wonder how this graph might have looked if the pandemic had never happened. Would we still see the same trends, or would some of these activities have remained stable or even decreased? Another question I have is what specifically caused religion and spirituality to grow so much between 2003 and 2022. Was it people searching for comfort during difficult times like the pandemic, or are there other cultural or societal shifts at play?
    For my community, it was a similar story. Being at home so much brought changes to how we spent our time and connected with others, which made these shifts in behavior very systemic. 
    
    New Title: The changing ways Americans spend their time at home.

raw_comment:
Firstly, I noticed that American adults engaging in religion and spirituality has increased significantly since 2003, rising from around 25% in 2003 to around 60% in 2022.  This is the largest increase in at-home activity participation seen on the graph.  I also noticed that all of the activities on the graph have increased.  I noticed that leisure (not on computer) has the highest percentage, at around 85% in 2022.  This surprises me because of the use of technology today, especially computers and other electronics.  Because of COVID-19, American adults as well as people all over the world began to spend more time at home, adjusting to a new lifestyle.  This could be the reason why all of these activities have had increased percentages of engagement at home for American adults.  I wonder if this graph would look different if the pandemic had never happened.  I also wonder why exactly religion and spirituality have increased significantly from 2003-2022.  This relates to me and my community because during the pandemic, I participated in all of these activities at home.  Personally, I participated in these activities at home more during the pandemic than ever before in my life.  
    Headline: America's Favorite at Home Activities

| 2003 value | Quantitative | X-position of open circle marker |
| 2022 value | Quantitative | X-position of arrowhead endpoint |

Notes:
- The blue line/arrow connects the two yearly values for each activity, visually encoding **change over time**.
raw_comment:
Headline: Living Room Revolution: Home Activities Take Over!
    
    The percentage of people doing activities at home has increased for each activity since 2003. I think the graph is trying to explain how life has changed throughout the years. Back in 2003, way fewer people did activities at home as they do now. This is due to the advancement of technology and the things that COVID-19 introduced us to. I wonder if Covid never happened and if working from home would still have become more popular. I also wonder why there has been such a significant shift in religion and spirituality, which is becoming more of a home activity. I wonder if social change throughout the years led to this shift. This relates to my community and me because I have grown in a time when technology has played an enormous role, as well as COVID-19. I have seen the effects of COVID-19 on jobs. My dad used to work in person part-time; however, after COVID-19, he now works hybrid.

raw_comment:
I notice that leisure is the most time-consuming activity. Additionally, religion and spirituality showed the most dramatic increase, jumping from 30% to 60% over the span of 19 years. I. wonder why the graph does not include leisure with technology, considering how much of our time at home is spent engaging with digital devices. It seems like leisure activities with tech (like streaming, gaming, or social media) would account for a significant portion of time, yet they are excluded. I also wonder if the increase in religion and spirituality is tied to global events, such as the pandemic or societal shifts towards introspection and mental health. How much of this time is due to changes in work-life balance, and how much is influenced by technology allowing people to engage with leisure or spiritual activities from home? This graph is particularly relevant to me because I’ve noticed these shifts in my own routines and those of people around me—more time spent on hobbies, self-care, and home-centered activities.

raw_comment:
This graph displays the increase in time spent doing at-home activities compared to outdoor activities between 2003 and 2022. All at-home activities increased during this time period. This means that people are spending less time doing activities outside of their homes. For example, religion and spirituality became much more home-centered. This means that many people decide to stay home and practice their religions instead of going out to church. The decline of leaving the home to participate in activities could decrease socialization and community in the population. I wonder what the largest contributing factor is in the decline of outdoor activities. This relates to my community because if people continue to be outside less, there will be less participation in my community. 
    Headline: Get Outside!

Headline: "Work from Home or Life from Home? Activities from Home Are on the Rise!
    
    This graph depicts on average how often American adults do a certain activity at home. One thing I noticed is that leisure (not on a computer) has the highest percentage of activities at home in 2003 and 2022, exceeding 80%. I also noticed that religion and spirituality have increased the most from 2003-2022 from about 25% to 60% at home. I wonder why religion and spirituality from home have increased so much over the past years. Perhaps it may be because people were seeking comfort in religion/ spirituality during COVID-19 and now that things are open again they realized they like it more from home. This graph relates to me and my community because we are now in a time where adults can work from home and stay home more. Adults can now have more time for activities like religion, spirituality, and leisure while working from home or hybrid.

raw_comment:
When looking at this graph on activities in the home, I noticed a couple of things. First, leisure has stayed consistently high and raised a little over 5% from 2003-2022. Also, religion and spirituality have grown from 20% to around 60%, which is the biggest growth demonstrated on this chart. I also noticed that there are a couple of activities listed in the description not on the graph like sleeping and shopping, that align with the hobbies of ages 15-18(the sample was ages 15 and over). My biggest curiosity about this graph is if the recent COVID-19 lockdown contributed to the rise in some of the activities done at home like work and education. I also wonder how much these activities rose each year so then it might be easier to theorize on what caused spikes. For example, is the introduction of new and better technology a reason why some of these things are done at home?  This impacts me and my community because I have grown up ina. time period where technology is a huge part of our daily life and makes it so more things can be done at home. During the lockdown in 2020 I spent a lot of time in my own home and learned how to accomplish certain things from there which has made my life easier. 
    
    Heading: Homebodies: How are people spending their time at home?

1) When looking at the graph, the first thing I notice is the increases from 2003-2022 for all the activities. Specifically, Religion and Spirituality has had the highest jump out of the 6 activities listed. The respondents of this graph are 15 and over as well. I  also noticed that under the graph it says that there were numerous other responses that were not included. Finally, I noted that under the graph it says that these responses were gathered via telephone survey.
    2) In my prior sentence, I learned that the survey was conducted through the phone. I wonder if this method would alter the responses as older people are more likely to pick up the phone than younger, effecting the 15 and over range. I also wonder why they chose to include these 6 activities specifically. Finally, I wonder how these responses would change in 2024-2025.

I think that a lot of those habits, that we picked up through the pandemic, have stuck with us whether it is good or bad.

This relates to me because I spend a lot of time at home, and I think that everyone staying at home isolates the community in a negative way. I think that as a community everyone should do their best to be social and get out of the house more.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
    This graph shows how people spent their time at home from 2003 to 2024. Since 2003, the biggest increase in activity was religion and spirituality. In 2003, only about 20% of Americans practiced religion and spirituality at home. Now, it has increased to around 60%. I also noticed that leisure has been the highest activity from 2003 to 2024. The least average in 2003 was work, although that has increased from 15% of Americans to 25% since then. 
    What do you wonder?
    I wonder why home activities such as religion, education, and work have increased significantly since 2003. Does it have to do with the COVID-19 pandemic and people changing their lifestyles to adapt to it? I also wonder why they asked Americans ages 15 years or older if this graph is more targeted toward adults. 
    How does this relate to you and your community?
    This relates to me and my community because since the pandemic, my parents and many others have switched to mostly remote work. As a society, we have begun to normalize staying home for the convenience of it.

image_description:
## 1) Chart type
- **Horizontal dumbbell / arrow range chart** comparing two time points per activity category.

## 2) Layout techniques
- Uses **one row per activity** (categorical grouping on the y-axis).
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Not stacked.
- Each row shows a **start point and end point connected by a horizontal arrow**, indicating change from **2003** to **2022**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Activity category (e.g., Leisure, Eating and drinking, Religion and spirituality, Education, Sports and exercise, Work) | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis; text labels |
| Share of time spent at home on activity | Quantitative | Position on x-axis |
| Year (2003 vs 2022) | Temporal | Endpoint role within each arrowed segment; labeled start/end markers |
| 2003 value | Quantitative | X-position of open circle marker |
| 2022 value | Quantitative | X-position of arrowhead endpoint |

Notes:
- The blue line/arrow connects the two yearly values for each activity, visually encoding **change over time**.
raw_comment:
What do I notice?  I notice that in the past 15 years, the majority of time at home is now spent as leisure, which means chilling and relaxing. However, the time spent practicing religion has significantly increased as well. I notice that the time spent eating and drinking has also increased in the past few years.
    What do I wonder? I wonder what has caused  religion and spirituality to increase. Maybe it is ue to covid, and the free time everyone had during this time. I also wonder if the time spent as leisure has also increased due to covid, because people had so much time to spend at home. 
    What do I think is going on in this graph?  I think this graph is showing the time spent at home doing certain activities. The graph is showing what activities have increased in the past few years, and which ones have stayed the same. I notice that religion has increased the most, and sports the least. 
    How does this relate to you and your community? This graph relates to my community because i personally spend a lot of my time at home chilling, and not really doing anything. I also like to spend my time eating, and making food. However, i don't really spend my time at home practicing my religion.

raw_comment:
This graph shows how people do certain things in their homes. I noticed that there were no decreases in any of these categories. This could be due to the increase in technology in the past twenty years. There could also be a connection to the COVID-19 pandemic. More people started working at home, and religious congregations began to be live-streamed. I wonder if the lack of decreases in any categories is purposeful or simply reflexive on how people are more isolated now than twenty years ago. I spend a lot of time at home because of my phone's convenience. I do not have to go anywhere to do schoolwork because everything I need is on my computer. With eating and drinking, the rise in apps such as DoorDash allows people to stay at home but not cook.
    
    Title: Everything you need at your home, but at what cost?

raw_comment:
1. I observe that the average time spent on various activities has increased across the board from 2003 to 2022, including leisure, eating and drinking, religion and spirituality, education, sports and exercise, and work. Notably, there has been a surprising and significant rise in time dedicated to religion and spirituality. Interestingly, while work and education have also seen increases, leisure time has paradoxically grown as well.
    2. The significant increase in religion and spirituality raises questions about the factors driving this trend, especially in light of the recent growth of atheism. Additionally, I wonder about the criteria used to define religious or spiritual activities performed at home.
    3. This observation resonates with me and my community, as it provides a fairly accurate reflection of how the average American, including those in my circle, allocates their time. It could also be connected to broader issues, such as rising rates of depression and a declining happiness index.
    4. Tracing Time: Unpacking Shifts in American Daily Activities and Their Societal Implications

raw_comment:
Welcome to Wednesday's live moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  Today’s graph is about Americans becoming more “homebodies” based on what share of the time they spend on an activity is at home.   Do you find that you and your family members are more homebodies than in the past?  Of the time spent at home, what share is by yourself rather than with family or friends?
    
    From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online for the four questions.  If you include a claim, please back it up with evidence that supports your claim.     I noticed from 2003 to 2022 all home activities have increased. I also noticed that religion increased most of all the activities.  Leisure and work increased the least.
    What do you wonder?
    I wonder why this type of graph was shown to convey this info. I wonder how this information was collected and how accurate it is. I wonder if the increase in work has anything to do with the increase of working at home. 
    How does this relate to you and your community?
    This relates to me because many people around me began working from home during the pandemic. This would directly change what's going on in this graph as time at home went to basically 100% during this time. 
    Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
    Americans a day in their life.

raw_comment:
1. I was really surprised that the activity that saw the largest increase in at-home engagement was religion and spirituality. The percentage of time increased from roughly 25-60% in Religion, which was far greater than any other category. I also noticed that the change in the percentage of work at home was one of the least significant changes. I was surprised by this and would have expected a much larger jump, given we had the pandemic, which changed the dynamic of the workplace for many companies.
    2. I really wonder what it was that caused the practice of religion and spirituality at home to spike so much during this time period. Is it because we live in a more diverse nation now with increasing religious variety? What changes in our society led us to this increase?
    3. The information here relates to me because, as someone born in the mid-2000s, this graph almost exactly covers the course of my lifetime. It is really interesting to see how our society and habits have evolved from the time I first entered this world to my now adult self.
    4. The Homebodys of America: What Are They Really Doing?

raw_comment: This graph displays several types of activities people 15 years of age or older do at home using percentages from 2003 and 2022. The year ranges are completely different which can provide differing results because of different trends, new technology, etc. I noticed that leisure was already at a high percentage in 2003 and continued to increase in 2022. This surprised me because I would have assumed that people would mainly be spending their time on their phones, computers, etc. instead of doing things outside of technology. I also saw how religion and spirituality skyrocketed. This may be because of world events and pandemics that cause people to be more in tune with religion and develop their faith. I wonder why work is at a low percentage for 2022 because, after the 2020 pandemic, many people were still working from home during this time. This relates to my community and myself because it shows how we do many different activities during our time at home and how they range in length. A headline could be: “The increase of homebody activities.”

raw_comment:
1) Observations - This graph shows the change in the percentage of time certain activities were done at home rather than outside from 2003 to 2022. Out of all the activities, religion & spirituality increased the most, with a 40% increase, meaning that on average, the Americans from the survey partook in religious/spiritual activities at home 60% of the time by 2022. Sports & Exercise, leisure time, eating & drinking had minor increases, while work & education had moderate increases. 
    
    2) Questions - I wonder why religious and spirituality activities show very high increases, and why sports, exercise, and leisure time only show minor increases. How does the increase of religious and spiritual practices at home impact traditional places of worship (i.e, church) or community gatherings? Could the increase in at-home activities contribute to loneliness and social isolation? Can we associate this with mental illness trends? 
    
    3) Relation to Community - Perhaps the significant increase in religious & spiritual practices at home could reflect how local religious communities have begun to use virtual services, signaling a change in how the people of NJ approach their faith. Additionally, if more people continued to move towards remote work & education, this could potentially decrease the demand for transportation.
    
    4) Headline - America Indoors: A Glimpse Into the Two-Decade Shift Toward Home-Centered Living!

raw_comment:
What do I notice?  I notice that people have started Working more in their free time.  The number is still low, but it has gone up significantly in the past 20 years.  I also notice that religion and spirituality have SOARED in the time frame.
    
    What do I wonder?  I wonder if the work people are starting to do more could be considered forms of hobbies that they get paid for.  I understand that people monetize their hobbies, and I would love to know if an increase in monetized hobbies has affected this graph.  I also wonder if spirituality plays the largest role in the Religion and Spirituality group increasing.  What if religious practices have stayed fairly similar, but spiritual practices (a pretty loose description) have increased?  That'd be cool.  
    
    How does this relate to my community and I?  Education, has clearly risen, and I feel like this is very noticeable in my community.  My brother and I have both started to apply ourselves more in school, and nearing college, many of my friends have began to step it up as well for that sweet GPA boost.  I'd like to see this education boost apply itself more in my own community, especially if some of my friends stay around where I live after graduating and find meaningful careers that support our neighbors.
    
    Catchy Headline :
    
    Activity Goes Domestic! - American Adults Beginning to Spend More Time at Home on Average

raw_comment:
I noticed that Religion and spirituality have experienced the most noticeable growth, although still remaining not too large. On the other hand, eating & drinking, sports, and leisure have sustained a fairy constant rate, showing little change over time.
    I wonder what factors have caused religion to gain more importance in recent years compared to 2003. I’m also curious about why education hasn’t expanded as much as others appear to show.
    This relates to me and my community since I’ve observed a growing focus on fitness, with more adults making gym visits and regular exercise a priority. At the same time, attending church or engaging in religious practices remains a weekly tradition for many people I know.
    My title for this topic would be, "The core of American Household priorities".

What did you notice? - Some of the things that I noticed about the graph were that some activities didn’t really change much in popularity as time went by such as leisure, eating/drinking, and sports. I also noticed that religious practices increased by a large margin and grew more than all of the other hobbies.
    
    What do you wonder? - I wonder why religion has become the most prevalent activity for home activities. I also wondered and had suspicion of why they used this type of line graph which is pretty old fashioned when bar graphs could have been used to interpret this data more easily. Again, I also wondered if this data is most likely accurate since it isn’t relying on a multi-day experiment and if genders had a role in contributing to these observations.
    
    Relationship to Community - I felt most of these occurrences of home activities becoming more frequent among society was due to the impact of quarantine during the COVID-19 pandemic which ended up closing major business locations like the gym, mall, and, particularly religious places (churches and mosques). But as of right now, I have seen and talked to people that have gone to the gym for a workout but haven’t seen many people talking about the place they pray (Church on Sundays for example).
    
    Catchy Headline - Societal Wars: Habits of the Adults

raw_comment:
I notice that the largest change in time each American adult spent at home on certain activities occurred with religion and spirituality. Although time on every activity at home increased, many increased by ~10%-20% from 2003 to 2022, but religion and spirituality had a jump of around 40% over the same time frame.
    I wonder if the increase in education and working from home was due to the COVID-19 pandemic. During the pandemic, lots of people switched from in-person education and going to the office to working and learning from home. The other thing I wonder is if the large change in religion and spirituality was due to the pandemic. During the pandemic, many people felt like the world was out of their control and were looking for both something to blame and something to believe in. I wonder if that contributed to the large jump in increased religion and spirituality.
    This relates to my community because I was a part of the generation that had to switch to learning from home so I have seen the change in all in-person education to a hybrid model and the disappearance of days like snow days, favoring a digital-learning model instead.
    My catchy headline is: America's at-home hobbies: How America has become more religious since 2003.

raw_comment:
I noticed that most American adults spend most of their time at home for leisure (free time). 80% + of the time is spent doing leisure. I also noticed that religion and spiruality became a lot more common in 2022, than it was in 2003. Work is the least common activity with the lowest percentages in 2003 and 2022. 
    I wonder what the reason was for the large increase in religion and spirituality percentages from 2003 to 2022. I also wonder if COVID was a factor that contributed to the percentages in the graph. I wonder if certain activities became more popular due to COVID. 
    This relates to me and my community because a lot of these activities are done in my home and my general community. I know lots of parents now just work from home due to the covid effect, so this could match up with the increase in the "work" percentage from 2003 to 2022. 
    Catchy headline: Popular at home activities over the years: what was the effect?
ace_sentences: Most American adults spend most of their time at home for leisure.
Eighty percent or more of the time is spent doing leisure.

     What do you wonder about?
    I wonder if this has to do with all the new diseases that have come to the surface. I also wonder what has increased religion over the years. I wonder why sports and exercise haven’t improved over the years.

1. What do you notice? The first thing I noticed about this graph was the way it was set up. I noticed that the circle section of the arrows look to represent the percentages from 2003 and the end of the arrow represents the percentage from 2022. Along with that, I couldn't help but notice the growth in the percentage of religion and spirituality. This was the sole activity that had the largest growth from 2003 to 2022. 
    
    2. What do you wonder? To add on the idea of religion and spirituality having the largest growth over the period of time, I wonder what events in this period of time caused that growth to occur. Part of me feels that it would be technology and COVID-19 related. 
    
    3. How does it relate to you or your community? This graph caused me to reflect on my personal daily activities. I noticed that as a high school student, my graph would have a higher percentage of time spent on Education, Eating and Drinking, and Work. It is interesting to me though that I feel my community around me would fit this graph, especially the religious aspect. I have noticed recently that people within my community have become more religious. 
    
    4. Create a headline: The 2003-2022 Percentage Differences of Time Spent by American Adults doing Activities at Home.

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Activity category (e.g., Leisure, Eating and drinking, Religion and spirituality, Education, Sports and exercise, Work) | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis; text labels |
| Share of time spent at home on activity | Quantitative | Position on x-axis |
| Year (2003 vs 2022) | Temporal | Endpoint role within each arrowed segment; labeled start/end markers |
| 2003 value | Quantitative | X-position of open circle marker |
| 2022 value | Quantitative | X-position of arrowhead endpoint |

Notes:
- The blue line/arrow connects the two yearly values for each activity, visually encoding **change over time**.
